title: Unusual Mass Mortality of Atlantic Puffins (Fratercula arctica) Associated to a Climatic Adverse Event in the Canary Islands
content: The Atlantic puffin (Fratercula arctica) is a charadriiform bird characterized by great diving capabilities, and transoceanic migratory behavior. These movements contribute to the dispersion of the species during migration, and episodes of mortality associated with migration may be a normal event in the dynamic of the Atlantic puffin populations. This study aimed to describe the anatomopathological findings of an unusual mortality event of Atlantic puffins observed during late 2022 and early 2023 along the coast of the Canary Islands. The most consistent gross finding during necropsy was generalized muscle atrophy and fat depletion. Main histological findings centered in the urinary tract with dilation and inflammation of the primary ureter branch and medullary cones, and intraluminal trematodes identified as Renicola sloanei based on morphology and molecular analysis. Influenza virus infection was ruled out in this mortality. The postmortem investigations performed in this mortality event of Atlantic puffins indicates that the animals were severely emaciated and suffered from nephropathy. The etiopathological investigation performed in this mortality event of Atlantic puffins indicates starvation associated with bad weather conditions during a migratory movement as the most likely cause of the unusual mortality event.
